intentAndPurpose.intent: Non-interactive display component used to highlight status, provide notifications, or categorize content. Supports start/end slots for icons and sub-badges.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Multi-accent appearance role. `'auto'` or omit: inherit nearest `<Surface>` effective role, else `sparkle`.

props.name: attention
props.description: Figma attention level — high (bold fill), medium (tinted fill), low (transparent). Default: 'high'.

props.name: children
props.description: Text content displayed inside the badge (Figma content=text → children).

props.name: end
props.description: Content to render after the label (icon, avatar, counter badge, indicator badge)

props.name: start
props.description: Content to render before the label (icon, avatar, counter badge, indicator badge)

interactionBehavior.summary: Badge is presentational, not a control: no hover, press, or focus styles, no click handler, and no tab stop. It renders a `<span role="status">` so assistive tech treats it as a status update rather than a button, and it inherits the parent's cursor — nest it inside a Chip, IconButton, or nav item and the parent's pointer and keyboard behaviour are what fire. A decorative `::after` overlay is taken out of hit-testing, so a tap on the Badge still activates that parent. The Badge itself does not set `data-surface`; filled `start` / `end` slots do, so slotted icons remapping is scoped to the slot. Explicit cross-role CounterBadge or IndicatorBadge children are wrapped in `data-context-boundary` so they keep their own role colour instead of picking up the Badge's.
